input.headline: Show a file the way it was before the work session next to the way it is now, compared line by line, instead of only a pile of one-edit-at-a-time blocks.
input.today: Open a file that a run of work changed and you see it as it stands on disk, with a separate block for each individual step that touched it. Ten edits are ten blocks, and anything that changed the file after the last of those steps — a formatter tidying it up, say — shows up in none of them. There is no single view of the file against what it looked like before the run started.
input.after: The same file also opens as one comparison: its text from before the run on one side, its text as it is now on the other, matched up line by line with the line numbers of both sides. Only the stretches that differ are shown, with three unchanged lines of context around each; the rest is folded away. It appears in one column first, with a toggle for two columns. A file that was created has nothing on the "before" side; a file that was deleted has nothing on the "now" side. A file past a line-count ceiling gets no comparison at all, and the screen says so rather than showing nothing.
steps: Take the "before" text from RG280's answer: a reader placed beside originOf hands back that answer's originalFile, which is empty when the run created the file.
Take the "now" text from the read the viewer (RG245) already performs, so whatever changed the file after the last call counts too; a file the run deleted is an empty side, every line removed.
Write linesBetween(before, after) in core as a pure line comparison: it returns hunks carrying line numbers for both sides, keeps three unchanged lines around each hunk, and folds the rest away.
Give it a ceiling on lines: past that ceiling, build no comparison at all, and have the viewer say so.
Draw the comparison in this project rather than reaching for BentoDiff: compare by line, show the numbers, default to inline, and offer side by side as a toggle.
Land it where the file is already shown — the viewer (RG245) with each call's two halves above it (RG246) — so the one comparison sits with the many per-call blocks.

terms.said: The tool that keeps this project's backlog; RG282 is one line in it, and the payload quoted above is roadkeep's own answer about that line.
One task in that backlog, written as a single line with an id, a status, the symptom it fixes and why it matters.
The status RG282 carries: it has a written design section (the §RG282 quoted in the payload) and has not shipped yet.
The group of the backlog this line belongs to.
Lines that have to be in place before this one can be built. RG282 has one: RG280.
A run of work over files that this app shows; the comparison is the file against how it was before that run began.
One step inside a session. The viewer already shows each call's two halves, so ten edits produce ten blocks.
The part that shows a file as the disk currently has it; RG245 is the line it came from.
The line behind the per-call blocks — each call's two halves, shown above the file.

originOf is an answer that already exists; originalFile is the field on it holding the file as it was before the session, empty for a file the session created. A reader sitting beside originOf is what hands it over.
The new pure comparison this task adds: given two texts, it works out what differs, line by line.
One stretch of the comparison where the two sides differ, carrying the line numbers of both sides, with three unchanged lines kept around it.
Everything outside those hunks is left out of the view rather than shown.
A limit on how many lines will be compared; past it, nothing is compared and the viewer says so.
The half of this project that holds pure rules — where linesBetween goes.
A ready-made comparison component the design explicitly does not use here; this view is drawn in the project instead.
Two layouts of the same comparison. The design asks for inline first, with side by side available as a toggle.
A standing rule the line is held to — something this work must not do, whatever else it does.
A file one of the non-goals forbids this task from writing to.

risks: originalFile is empty for a file the session created, so one side of the comparison legitimately has nothing in it.
A file the session deleted is an empty side with every line removed — the opposite edge case, and it has to read as such.

The "now" side is the disk's current text, not a snapshot at the last call, so anything that changed the file afterwards is inside the comparison. That is the point of the task, and it means the comparison is not tied to the calls.
Past the ceiling on lines no comparison is built at all, so the viewer needs something to say in its place.
The view is drawn in this project rather than with BentoDiff, so the line-by-line layout, the numbers and the inline/side-by-side toggle are all this task's own work.
